title: Lagged four-week broad U.S. dollar weakness DRA V1 entry admission
thesis: A falling broad U.S. dollar may identify easier global dollar-liquidity and risk-appetite conditions in which unchanged long DRA momentum entries have better realized breadth and inventory paths. Vetoing new parent entries while the broad dollar is not weaker than four weeks earlier may improve equal-capital DRA economics without altering exits or existing lots.
mechanism: Aggregate official DTWEXBGS weekday observations into calendar weeks ending Friday. Beginning five calendar days after Friday 00:00 UTC and for at most 168 hours, admit an otherwise unchanged DRA V1 parent signal only when the current weekly mean is strictly below the exact weekly mean 28 calendar days earlier; otherwise veto the new entry and leave all existing lots and exits untouched.
economic_rationale: The feature is useful only if it improves both Design and Validation total and realized PnL, preserves unrealized PnL, drawdown, underwater duration, holding and terminal inventory, intervenes often enough, and has annual and independent predictive breadth. Reduced market exposure, one favorable dollar regime or terminal inventory cleanup is insufficient.
